kurz: How interest rates influence purchase prices, what price statistics can tell you and how to assess a local market without relying on listings.
marken: Turn in the interest rate cycle

bloecke.md:
Two figures describe the German property cycle of the last one and a half decades. From 2010 to 2025, one- and two-family houses and flats in Germany became around 82% more expensive. This figure from the house price index covers newly built and existing properties, in each case including the land. Construction prices for residential buildings, which cover only the structure, rose by around 89% over the same period, and prices for owner-occupied housing by around 90% (Federal Statistical Office, Destatis). Purchase prices thus rose roughly to the same extent as construction costs. The rise therefore cannot be explained by pure speculation, because construction costs rose at the same pace. Nor can it be explained purely by costs being passed on, because from 2022 prices fell significantly although construction costs continued to rise.

Both explanations are incomplete because they leave out the interest rate as a third factor. The interest rate determines what purchase price a household can finance with a fixed monthly instalment. Since 2022, it has changed more than construction costs and rents combined.

bloecke.titel: House price index for Germany, change on the same quarter of the previous year
bloecke.unter: The chart shows only three documented quarterly values and no smoothed long-term series. The recovery after the price decline has recently slowed considerably. Source: Federal Statistical Office.

serien.name: Change on the same quarter of the previous year

bloecke.md:
This lesson deliberately does not show a continuous annual series from 2010 to 2026. In June 2026, the Federal Statistical Office rebased the house price index to 2025 = 100. Old and new index levels therefore cannot be chained together without conversion. You can retrieve the complete series yourself via GENESIS-Online (tables 61262 and 61261) and should not mix two base years in one chart. The figures on the depth of the 2022/2023 decline also differ widely depending on source, segment and region. What is documented is that prices are now rising again, but recently only slightly.

Regardless of data quality, every price index has a limitation. It is based on the properties sold in the period in question. Because these differ from quarter to quarter in construction year, size, location and features, the Federal Statistical Office uses a hedonic method to strip out the influence of such characteristics. In this way, a quarter with many renovated old buildings in good locations is not supposed to push the index up through its composition alone. The result, however, remains an average across all regions and property types. For your own purchase decision, the national index therefore only provides background information and no basis for the decision.

## Turn in the interest rate cycle and affordable purchase price

A purchase price is rarely negotiated in euros per square metre; buyers almost always think in monthly instalments. The household's income limits how high the instalment can be. How much loan can be financed with this instalment depends on the interest rate. With an [[Annuity loan (Annuitätendarlehen)|annuity loan (Annuitätendarlehen)]], the first instalment consists of interest and initial repayment. The amount that can be financed can be calculated directly from this.

bloecke.formel: Loan = Annual instalment / (Borrowing rate + Initial repayment)
bloecke.erklaerung: The formula is the annuity formula for the starting point, rearranged for the loan. Banks calculate monthly, so the effective interest rate is slightly above the borrowing rate. For the order of magnitude, an annual view is sufficient.
variablen: twelve monthly instalments that the household can afford permanently
nominal interest rate of the loan, not the effective interest rate
repayment rate in the first year, usually 2% to 3%
bloecke.beispiel: €1,500 a month, 2% initial repayment, 1% interest: 18,000 / 0.03 = €600,000. At 4% interest: 18,000 / 0.06 = €300,000.

bloecke.titel: Affordable loan amount with a monthly instalment of €1,500
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with a constant 2% initial repayment, annual view. If the interest rate rises from 1% to 4%, the amount that can be financed halves, although nothing has changed in the household.

bloecke.md: This calculation explains the development from 2022 onwards. Demand collapsed because, within a short time, the same households could only take out half as much in loans. The desire for housing, by contrast, had not diminished. Prices nevertheless fell considerably less than financing capacity, and this was due to the supply side. Owners under no pressure to sell would rather not offer their property than accept a discount. At the same time, new construction, which would have to fill the gap, became more expensive. The result was a sluggish market with few transactions, but without a crash.

bloecke.titel: Mortgage rates by length of fixed-rate period, as of 3 September 2026
bloecke.unter: Longer interest rate certainty costs a premium. The effective interest rate rises from 3.93% with a five-year fixed-rate period to 4.48% with a thirty-year one. Source: Dr. Klein, effective interest rate p.a.

kurven.name: Effective interest rate by fixed-rate period

bloecke.md: With a ten-year fixed-rate period, the offer rate according to the mortgage broker Dr. Klein was around 3.97% effective at the beginning of September 2026. According to the same source, borrowers with good creditworthiness and a low [[Loan-to-value ratio (Beleihungsauslauf)|loan-to-value ratio]] obtained best rates of about 3.6% to 3.8%. In October 2026, the broker expected best rates of between 4.0% and 4.5% for ten-year loans until the end of the year. That is an expectation and not a fact, and interest rate forecasts are often far off in both directions. Only the shape of the interest rate curve is reliable. A long fixed-rate period costs a premium; a short one shifts the interest rate risk to the follow-up financing.

## Price-to-rent ratio and rental yield

Any price level can be checked against the rent. The [[Price-to-rent ratio|price-to-rent ratio]] is the purchase price divided by the annual net basic rent. It is the reciprocal of the gross yield and therefore the quickest way to put a price into context. A factor of 25 corresponds to 4% gross, a factor of 40 to only 2.5%. However, the gross figure is only suitable for rough sorting, because incidental purchase costs and non-recoverable costs are missing from it.

The following calculation assumes a flat of 70 square metres with a net basic rent of €10 per square metre, that is, €8,400 in annual rent. The official guide values are deducted from this. For the maintenance of a building aged 32 years or more, this has been €18.62 per square metre per year under Section 28 II. BV (Second Computation Ordinance) since 1 January 2026 (€1,303.40), and for the rent loss allowance (Mietausfallwagnis) 2% under Section 29 II. BV (€168). This leaves €6,928.60. On the cost side, 8% incidental purchase costs are added, namely 6.5% [[Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer)|real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer)]] and around 1.5% for the notary and the land register. This corresponds to a purchase without an estate agent in a federal state with a high real estate transfer tax rate.

bloecke.titel: Price-to-rent ratio, price and yield for 70 m² and €8,400 annual net basic rent
Net rental yield compared with the mortgage rate
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation from the table, before tax and before financing. Only below a factor of about 19 is the property yield above the interest rate that the bank charges for a ten-year fixed-rate period.

bloecke.md: [[Leverage]] magnifies the effect of the difference between the property yield and the loan interest rate, in both directions. At a factor of 30, the net yield in this calculation is 2.55% and the interest rate for a ten-year fixed-rate period is 3.97%. Every borrowed euro then lowers the return on equity instead of raising it. From a debt share of about 64% of total costs, the purchase only pays off through an increase in value, and nobody can guarantee that. In the major cities, this has been the usual business model for years. In locations with factors below about 19, by contrast, the purchase pays for itself from the rent. Whether property is expensive in general is therefore less important than the question of which part of the expected return comes from the rent and which from a hoped-for increase in value.

## Taxation of property and portfolio

The comparison with the capital market is incomplete as long as it is made before tax. Rental surpluses are income from letting and leasing (Einkünfte aus Vermietung und Verpachtung) and are taxed at the personal tax rate. The marginal tax rate of 42% applies in 2026 from €69,879 of taxable income, that of 45% from €277,826 (Section 32a EStG, Income Tax Act). Capital income, by contrast, is subject to the [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] of 25% plus solidarity surcharge, together 26.375% (Section 32d(1) EStG). For equity funds, the partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) of 30% additionally reduces the tax base.

On sale, it is the other way round. The gain from selling a let property is tax-free after a holding period of ten years, the [[Speculation period (Spekulationsfrist)|speculation period (Spekulationsfrist)]] (Section 23 EStG; the dates of the notarised contracts are decisive). A price gain in the portfolio, by contrast, is subject to the flat-rate withholding tax even after thirty years. With accumulating funds, part of it is also taxed every year beforehand through the [[Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)|advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)]]. In 2026, the base interest rate (Basiszins) is 3.20%, so the advance lump sum is at most 2.24% of the value at the start of the year (Section 18 InvStG, Investment Tax Act). The property is therefore taxed more heavily on an ongoing basis and more lightly on sale. Depending on the holding period and marginal tax rate, the comparison can therefore come out in favour of one investment or the other.

## Supply, regions and demographics

On the supply side, the situation remains tight. Construction prices for residential buildings in May 2026 were 5.0% higher than a year earlier, after 3.3% in February. The increase is therefore accelerating again. The ifo business climate for residential construction stood at minus 22.7 points in August 2026, after minus 29.0. Expectations improved from minus 35.6 to minus 23.3. Sentiment remains negative but is improving with the rising number of building permits. For buyers, this means that new construction is becoming more expensive as an alternative. This limits the scope for falling prices of existing properties.

Regionally, the market consists of submarkets that have little to do with one another. In regions to which households are moving and where too little is being built, the rents justify even high factors. In regions whose population is ageing and moving away, by contrast, low purchase prices are not a bargain, because they reflect a foreseeable letting problem. This lesson deliberately does not contain reliable figures on migration and vacancy by district, because they quickly become outdated and are only meaningful locally. It is more important to know where to find them.

schritte.text: The locally responsible valuation committee (Gutachterausschuss), formed, depending on the federal state, for a district, an independent city, a municipality or a region, keeps a purchase price database (Kaufpreissammlung) of all notarised purchase contracts under Sections 192 et seq. BauGB (Federal Building Code). From this, it publishes market reports with transaction figures, price ranges and multipliers. They are based on the prices agreed in the contracts and are the only source of this kind.

The standard land value (Bodenrichtwert) under Section 196 BauGB can be accessed in the portals of the federal states (usually BORIS). It shows what share of the purchase price is attributable to the land. This also makes it the basis for the allocation that the tax office expects for depreciation.

schritte.titel: Compare the local rent index with the advertised rent
schritte.text: The qualified local rent index (qualifizierter Mietspiegel) under Sections 558c and 558d BGB (Civil Code) shows the local comparative rent. If the rent used in the calculation is well above it, the return calculation is based on a rent that may not stand up in court.

Count how many comparable properties are offered on the portal and how long they have already been listed there. Listings do not show prices paid, but the time on the market is a good early indicator of the room for negotiation.

The statistical offices of the federal states publish net migration, age structure and building permits for the district. Rising permits with a stagnating population are a warning sign for rents in the coming years.

The purchase price is divided by the achievable annual net basic rent, followed by the net calculation with maintenance and rent loss. Only the result of the net calculation can be compared with the interest rate that the bank charges.

bloecke.md: The national index describes an average that does not apply to any individual property. For a purchase decision, you need three local figures: the level of prices paid from the purchase price database, the local rent and your own financing rate. If the net rental yield is below this rate, the rest of the expected return is based on a hoped-for increase in value. You can buy on that basis too, but you should be aware of it.

The house price index and the construction price index are nominal series. With consumer price inflation above this figure, a rise of 0.6% on the previous year means that the purchasing power of the property falls in real terms. The price in euros does rise, but the quantity of goods you would get for it falls.

For owner-occupiers this is less significant, because in return they save a rent that rises with inflation. For buy-to-let investors, the point is central. A property only protects against inflation if rents are allowed to rise with other prices. In markets with the rent brake (Mietpreisbremse) and capped modernisation rent increases, this is restricted. Whether a property protects against inflation therefore depends on the tenancy law in the market concerned.

mitnehmen: The interest rate has the strongest influence on purchase prices, because with the same monthly instalment and 2% initial repayment, a rise from 1% to 4% halves the loan amount that can be financed.
From 2010 to 2025, purchase prices rose by around 82% and construction prices by around 89%, so that new construction offers no cheap alternative and prices of existing properties are supported.

The price-to-rent ratio is the reciprocal of the gross yield, and only after taking incidental purchase costs, maintenance and rent loss into account does it produce a figure that can be compared with the mortgage rate.
If the net rental yield is below the loan interest rate, leverage works against the buyer, and as the share of debt grows, the return depends more and more on an increase in value.
Local market conditions can be measured by the prices paid from the valuation committee's purchase price database, not by listings.

begriffe.text: Index of the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) for the price development of residential property. It covers the properties sold, including the land, uses a hedonic method to strip out the influence of characteristics such as size and location, and is regularly rebased to a new base year, most recently in June 2026 to 2025 = 100. Values with different base years must not be mixed.

Index of prices for the construction of new residential buildings. It describes the development of replacement costs excluding land; in regions with demand, rising construction prices also support the prices of existing properties. In May 2026, it was 5.0% above the same month of the previous year.

Collection of all notarised purchase contracts in a district, kept by the valuation committee (Gutachterausschuss) under Sections 192 et seq. BauGB. It is the basis of the property market reports and the standard land values and the only source of purchase prices paid.

Average location value of land per square metre, which the valuation committee determines at least every two years under Section 196 BauGB and which can be accessed via the portals of the federal states. It is used to split the purchase price into a land portion and a building portion.
